candidate.title: Coquitlam is hiring 250 election workers for October vote

evidence.readerImpact: Coquitlam residents can decide whether to apply for paid temporary election work and know the roles, pay ranges, training requirement, voting dates, and eligibility rules before applying.
evidence.freshnessEvidence: The City of Coquitlam posted the recruitment notice on July 23, 2026, the same day as this sweep.
evidence.uniqueAngleEvidence: Existing Trends Today Coquitlam coverage covers heat, road safety, storm drains, and signal work, but no 2026 local-election worker recruitment or election staffing application story.

candidate.lengthRationale: A bulletin is the shortest complete format because the reader job is a same-day official recruitment notice with roles, pay, dates, eligibility, and an application path.
candidate.commercialFitReason: The official source creates civic-participation and local temporary-work intent, but no verified Trends Today ad, sponsor, or RPM data supports treating this as a commercial story.
